Pathology 05.question: ১) Loss or suppression of cough reflex during anesthesia or coma leads to which type of pneumonia?
Pathology 05.exp:
During anesthesia or coma, the cough and protective airway reflexes are suppressed. This allows oropharyngeal or gastric contents to enter the lower respiratory tract, causing aspiration pneumonia. It commonly affects dependent portions of the lungs.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
Loss of gag/cough reflex → aspiration → aspiration pneumonia.
Common risk factors include coma, anesthesia, impaired consciousness, dysphagia, and neuromuscular disorders.

Exam pearl:
“Absent cough reflex = aspirate = aspiration pneumonia.”

Pathology 05.question: ২) Which is the most common joint disorder?
Pathology 05.exp:
Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common joint disorder and the most common form of arthritis. It is a degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive loss of articular cartilage, subchondral bone changes, and osteophyte formation.

High-yield Rheumatology recall:
Osteoarthritis: commonly affects the knees, hips, spine, and hands. Risk increases with age, obesity, previous joint injury, and mechanical stress.

Exam pearl:
Most common joint disorder = Osteoarthritis.

Pathology 05.question: ৩) Which bronchial carcinoma is radiosensitive?
Pathology 05.exp:
Small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) is highly radiosensitive and also highly chemosensitive. However, it is aggressive and commonly presents with early metastasis. Chemotherapy combined with radiotherapy is central to treatment in limited-stage disease.

High-yield Oncology recall:
SCLC → highly radiosensitive + chemosensitive → early metastasis.
In contrast, non-small-cell lung cancers (NSCLC) are generally less sensitive to chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

Exam pearl:
“Small cells are sensitive” → SCLC is the most radiosensitive bronchial carcinoma.

Pathology 05.question: ৪) Acute coronary syndrome excludes.....?
Pathology 05.exp:
Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) refers to acute myocardial ischemia due to sudden reduction in coronary blood flow. It classically includes unstable angina, NSTEMI, and STEMI. Chronic ischemic heart disease is a chronic condition and therefore is not classified as ACS.

Note: Sudden cardiac death is a possible complication of acute coronary ischemia but is not itself one of the three standard clinical categories of ACS.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
ACS = Unstable angina + NSTEMI + STEMI

Exam pearl:
“ACS is acute, not chronic” → Chronic ischemic heart disease is excluded.

Pathology 05.question: ৫) Predominant lymphocytes in pleural fluid study indicates....?
Pathology 05.exp:
A lymphocyte-predominant pleural effusion strongly suggests tuberculosis or malignancy. In regions where TB is common, tuberculous pleural effusion is a classic cause. TB pleural effusion is typically an exudative, lymphocyte-predominant effusion.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
Lymphocyte-predominant pleural effusion → TB, malignancy, lymphoma.
Neutrophil-predominant → acute bacterial infection/parapneumonic effusion.

Exam pearl:
“Lymphocytes in pleural fluid → think TB first” in a high-TB-prevalence setting.

Pathology 05.question: ৬) Which is not true about rheumatoid arthritis?
Pathology 05.exp:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by persistent synovial inflammation and progressive joint damage. It is not primarily an acute disease.

High-yield Rheumatology recall:
RA → chronic + autoimmune + inflammatory + systemic.
It can have extra-articular manifestations involving the lungs, eyes, skin, heart, and blood vessels.

Exam pearl:
RA is a chronic systemic inflammatory disease—not an acute disease.

Pathology 05.question: ৭) Inflammatory pleural effusion occurs in......?
Pathology 05.exp:
Pleuritis (pleurisy) is inflammation of the pleura and can produce an inflammatory pleural effusion, typically an exudative effusion. Common causes include infection, tuberculosis, malignancy, and autoimmune diseases.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
Inflammation of pleura → Pleuritis → Exudative pleural effusion.
By contrast, hydrothorax generally refers to a non-inflammatory, transudative pleural effusion.

Exam pearl:
“Pleuritis = inflamed pleura = inflammatory pleural effusion.”

Pathology 05.question: ৮) Which has association with HLA-B27?
Pathology 05.exp:
HLA-B27 is strongly associated with the seronegative spondyloarthropathies, particularly ankylosing spondylitis. Other associated conditions include reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and enteropathic arthritis.

High-yield Rheumatology recall:
HLA-B27 associations:

  • Ankylosing spondylitis

  • Reactive arthritis

  • Psoriatic arthritis

  • Enteropathic arthritis

Exam pearl:
HLA-B27 → think “seronegative spondyloarthropathy,” especially ankylosing spondylitis.

Pathology 05.question: ৯) Hospital acquired pneumonia is called.........?
Pathology 05.exp:
Hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) is also called nosocomial pneumonia. It is pneumonia that develops 48 hours or more after hospital admission and was not present or incubating at the time of admission.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
HAP = Nosocomial pneumonia
Important risk factors include prolonged hospitalization, mechanical ventilation, aspiration risk, and exposure to healthcare-associated pathogens.

Exam pearl:
“Hospital acquired = nosocomial.”

Pathology 05.question: ১০) Which is the cause of most of the cases of IHD?
Pathology 05.exp:
Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease is responsible for the vast majority of cases of ischemic heart disease (IHD). Atherosclerotic plaques narrow the coronary arteries and can rupture, causing thrombosis and acute coronary syndromes.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
Major risk factors for coronary atherosclerosis include smoking, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, obesity, and increasing age.

Exam pearl:
Most IHD = coronary atherosclerosis.

Pathology 05.question: ১১) Which organism is most common for atypical pneumonia?
Pathology 05.exp:
Mycoplasma pneumoniae is the classic and most common cause of atypical (walking) pneumonia, particularly in children, adolescents, and young adults. It commonly causes a gradual onset of dry cough, fever, and malaise.

High-yield Microbiology recall:
Mycoplasma pneumoniae lacks a cell wall, so β-lactam antibiotics are ineffective. Macrolides or doxycycline are commonly used when treatment is indicated.

Exam pearl:
Atypical pneumonia + young patient + dry cough → Mycoplasma pneumoniae.

Pathology 05.question: ১২) Gout is caused by excessive amount of......?
Pathology 05.exp:
Gout is caused by hyperuricemia, leading to deposition of monosodium urate crystals in joints and tissues. The crystals trigger intense inflammatory arthritis, classically affecting the first metatarsophalangeal joint (podagra).

High-yield Rheumatology recall:
Purine metabolism → uric acid → monosodium urate crystal deposition → gout.

Exam pearl:
Gout = hyperuricemia + monosodium urate crystals.

Pathology 05.question: ১৩) Which is not true about normal pleural fluid?
Pathology 05.exp:
Normal pleural fluid is a small amount of clear, serous fluid, usually around 10–20 mL, containing very few cells. It is not normally mucous. Mucous material suggests an abnormal process.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
Normal pleural fluid → small volume + clear/serous + few cells.

Exam pearl:
Normal pleural fluid is clear and serous, not mucous.

Pathology 05.question: ১৪) The major morphological manifestations of gout excludes........?
১৫) Which one is not acyanotic heart disease?
Pathology 05.exp:
Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is the classic cyanotic congenital heart disease due to right-to-left shunting caused by right ventricular outflow tract obstruction. Therefore, it is not an acyanotic heart disease.

PDA, ASD, and VSD are generally classified as acyanotic congenital heart diseases because they initially produce left-to-right shunts.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
Cyanotic CHD: TOF, transposition of great arteries, truncus arteriosus, tricuspid atresia, etc.
Acyanotic CHD: ASD, VSD, PDA, coarctation of aorta.

Exam pearl:
TOF = “Blue baby” → cyanotic congenital heart disease.

Pathology 05.question: ১৬) Which is not one of the four major modifiable factors of atherosclerosis?
Pathology 05.exp:
Family history is a non-modifiable risk factor for atherosclerosis. The major modifiable risk factors include hyperlipidemia, cigarette smoking, and hypertension; diabetes mellitus is also an important modifiable risk factor.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
Modifiable: smoking, hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, obesity, physical inactivity.
Non-modifiable: age, sex, and family history/genetic predisposition.

Exam pearl:
Family history = non-modifiable risk factor for atherosclerosis.

Pathology 05.question: ১৭) Pseudogout is related to excessive....... ?
Pathology 05.exp:
Pseudogout is caused by deposition of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystals in joints, producing acute inflammatory arthritis. It commonly affects the knee and wrist, especially in older adults.

High-yield Rheumatology recall:
Gout → monosodium urate crystals
Pseudogout → calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystals

Exam pearl:
“Pseudo = CPPD” → Pseudogout = calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease.

Pathology 05.question: ১৮) Painless myocardial ischemia may occur in....?
Pathology 05.exp:
Painless (silent) myocardial ischemia commonly occurs in patients with diabetes mellitus due to diabetic autonomic neuropathy, which can impair the perception of ischemic chest pain. Therefore, myocardial ischemia may occur without typical anginal symptoms.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
Diabetes → autonomic neuropathy → reduced pain perception → silent myocardial ischemia.

Exam pearl:
“Diabetic patients may not feel ischemia.” → Think silent/painless MI or ischemia.

Pathology 05.question: ১৯) Chronic necrotizing inflammation of bronchi & bronchioles associated with abnormal permanent dilation is called......?
Pathology 05.exp:
Bronchiectasis is characterized by permanent, abnormal dilation of the bronchi and bronchioles due to chronic infection and inflammation, with destruction of the bronchial wall. It commonly presents with chronic productive cough and recurrent respiratory infections.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
Bronchiectasis → permanent bronchial dilation + chronic inflammation/infection.

Exam pearl:
“Permanent dilation of bronchi = bronchiectasis.”

Pathology 05.question: ২০) Which cytokine plays a central role in RA?
Pathology 05.exp:
Tumor necrosis factor (TNF), particularly TNF-α, plays a central role in the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). It promotes synovial inflammation, stimulates other inflammatory cytokines, and contributes to cartilage and bone destruction.

High-yield Rheumatology recall:
TNF-α → major inflammatory mediator in RA.
This is why TNF inhibitors such as infliximab, adalimumab, and etanercept are important biological therapies for RA.

Exam pearl:
RA + central cytokine → TNF-α.

Pathology 05.question: ২১) Which of the following is not a pattern of angina?
Pathology 05.exp:
The recognized clinical patterns/types of angina include stable angina, unstable angina, and variant (Prinzmetal) angina. Paroxysmal angina is not a standard classification of angina.

High-yield Cardiology recall:

  • Stable angina → predictable, exertional, relieved by rest/nitroglycerin.

  • Unstable angina → new, worsening, or occurring at rest.

  • Prinzmetal (variant) angina → coronary vasospasm, typically at rest.

Exam pearl:
Stable + unstable + Prinzmetal = classic angina patterns; paroxysmal is not a standard type.

Pathology 05.question: ২২) Which is the commonest organism for CAP?
Pathology 05.exp:
Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common bacterial cause of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in adults. It commonly causes acute fever, productive cough, pleuritic chest pain, and may produce lobar consolidation.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
CAP → S. pneumoniae is the classic exam association.
Other causes include Haemophilus influenzae, atypical organisms such as Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and respiratory viruses.

Exam pearl:
“CAP’s classic culprit = S. pneumoniae.”

Pathology 05.question: ২৩) What type of emphysema usually occurs in cigarette smokers?
Pathology 05.exp:
Centriacinar emphysema is strongly associated with cigarette smoking. It predominantly affects the respiratory bronchioles and is usually more severe in the upper lobes.

Panacinar emphysema is classically associated with α₁-antitrypsin deficiency and tends to involve the lower lobes.

High-yield Respiratory recall:

  • Smoking → Centriacinar → Upper lobes

  • α₁-antitrypsin deficiency → Panacinar → Lower lobes

  • Paraseptal → Subpleural → Associated with spontaneous pneumothorax

Exam pearl:
“Cigarette = Centriacinar; A1AT deficiency = Panacinar.”

Pathology 05.question: ২৪) What type of necrosis occurs in myocardium in MI?
Pathology 05.exp:
Myocardial infarction (MI) causes ischemic injury, resulting in coagulative necrosis of cardiac muscle. The basic tissue architecture is initially preserved despite cellular death.

Liquefactive necrosis is more characteristic of brain infarction and abscesses, while caseous necrosis is classically associated with tuberculosis.

High-yield Pathology recall:
Ischemic necrosis → coagulative necrosis in most solid organs, including the heart, kidney, and spleen.
Exception: Brain infarction → liquefactive necrosis.

Exam pearl:
MI = coagulative necrosis; brain infarction = liquefactive necrosis.

Pathology 05.question: ২৫) Which is the major symptom of COPD?
Pathology 05.exp:
Dyspnea (breathlessness) is the major and most characteristic symptom of COPD, particularly exertional dyspnea that progressively worsens as airflow obstruction advances. Chronic cough and sputum production are also common, but dyspnea is the key symptom.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
COPD → progressive exertional dyspnea + chronic cough ± sputum production.

Exam pearl:
Progressive breathlessness in a smoker → think COPD.

Pathology 05.question: ২৬) CRP is positive in which IHD?
Pathology 05.exp:
C-reactive protein (CRP) is an acute-phase reactant that rises in response to systemic inflammation. Acute myocardial infarction (MI) can cause a significant inflammatory response, resulting in elevated CRP levels.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
Acute MI → inflammatory response → CRP may rise.
CRP, particularly high-sensitivity CRP (hs-CRP), is also used as a cardiovascular risk marker, but it is not specific for MI.

Exam pearl:
Acute MI can produce a positive/elevated CRP due to inflammation.

Pathology 05.question: ২৭) What type of hypersensitivity reactions occur in atopic asthma?
Pathology 05.exp:
Atopic asthma is primarily a Type I (immediate) hypersensitivity reaction, mediated by IgE. Allergen exposure causes IgE-mediated mast-cell activation, releasing mediators such as histamine and leukotrienes, leading to bronchoconstriction and airway inflammation.

High-yield Immunology recall:
Type I hypersensitivity → IgE → mast cells → allergy/anaphylaxis/atopic asthma.

Exam pearl:
Atopic asthma = Type I hypersensitivity = IgE-mediated.

Pathology 05.question: ২৮) Which CK level is increased in MI?
Pathology 05.exp:
CK-MB (creatine kinase–MB) is the CK isoenzyme most closely associated with cardiac muscle injury and rises after acute myocardial infarction (MI). It typically begins to rise within 3–6 hours, peaks around 24 hours, and returns toward normal within 48–72 hours.

High-yield Cardiology recall:

  • CK-MB → myocardial injury

  • Troponin I/T → more sensitive and specific for MI

  • CK-MM → skeletal muscle

  • CK-BB → brain and smooth muscle

Exam pearl:
MI → CK-MB rises; troponin is the preferred modern biomarker.

Pathology 05.question: ২৯) Which is an indifferentiated malignant epithelial tumor of lung?
Pathology 05.exp:
Large cell carcinoma is a poorly differentiated malignant epithelial tumor of the lung in which the malignant cells lack clear features of squamous or glandular differentiation. It is classified under non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC).

High-yield Oncology recall:
The major lung carcinoma categories include:

  • Squamous cell carcinoma

  • Adenocarcinoma

  • Small cell carcinoma

  • Large cell carcinoma

Large cell carcinoma → undifferentiated/poorly differentiated epithelial malignancy.

Exam pearl:
“No squamous or glandular differentiation → Large cell carcinoma.”

Pathology 05.question: ৩০) Pathological changes due to systemic hypertension occurs in........?
Pathology 05.exp:
Systemic hypertension increases afterload on the left ventricle, causing compensatory left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). Chronic hypertension can eventually lead to LV diastolic dysfunction, heart failure, and other cardiovascular complications.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
Systemic hypertension → ↑ afterload → LV hypertrophy → diastolic dysfunction.

Exam pearl:
Systemic hypertension primarily affects the LV because it pumps against systemic vascular resistance.

Pathology 05.question: ৩১) Which is not a cause of high output cardiac failure?
Pathology 05.exp:
High-output cardiac failure occurs when cardiac output is elevated or inappropriately high despite the development of heart failure. Classic causes include severe anemia, thyrotoxicosis, and large arteriovenous/intracardiac shunts.

Valvular incompetence can cause heart failure, but it is not a classic cause of high-output cardiac failure.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
Common causes of high-output cardiac failure:

  • Severe anemia

  • Thyrotoxicosis

  • Arteriovenous fistula

  • Beriberi (thiamine deficiency)

  • Paget disease of bone

  • Large intracardiac shunts

Exam pearl:
High-output failure → think “low systemic resistance or excessive demand”; valvular incompetence is not a classic cause.

Pathology 05.question: ৩২) What type of hypersensitivity reaction occurs in rheumatic heart disease?
Pathology 05.exp:
Rheumatic heart disease follows Group A Streptococcus infection and results from molecular mimicry. Antibodies generated against streptococcal antigens cross-react with host tissues, particularly cardiac tissue, producing an antibody-mediated (Type II) hypersensitivity reaction.

High-yield Immunology recall:
Rheumatic fever → molecular mimicry → cross-reactive antibodies → Type II hypersensitivity.

Exam pearl:
“Rheumatic heart disease = Type II hypersensitivity.”

Pathology 05.question: ৩৩) Oat cell carcinoma is a variant of which lung tumor?
Pathology 05.exp:
Oat cell carcinoma is the classic histological term for small cell carcinoma of the lung. The tumor consists of small cells with scant cytoplasm, hyperchromatic nuclei, and finely granular chromatin.

High-yield Oncology recall:
Small cell carcinoma = oat cell carcinoma.
It is a high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma, strongly associated with cigarette smoking and characterized by early metastasis.

Exam pearl:
“Oat cells = Small cells” → Oat cell carcinoma is SCLC.

Pathology 05.question: ৩৪) Which is a major criteria for diagnosis of rheumatic heart disease?
Pathology 05.exp:
Carditis is one of the major Jones criteria for diagnosing acute rheumatic fever, which can lead to rheumatic heart disease. The major criteria are carditis, migratory polyarthritis, Sydenham chorea, erythema marginatum, and subcutaneous nodules.

Fever, arthralgia, and raised ESR are minor criteria.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
Major Jones criteria:

  • Carditis

  • Migratory polyarthritis

  • Sydenham chorea

  • Erythema marginatum

  • Subcutaneous nodules

Exam pearl:
“Jones major = Carditis, Arthritis, Chorea, Erythema, Nodules.”

Pathology 05.question: ৩৫) Tuberculosis cannot affect the following except....?
Pathology 05.exp:
Tuberculosis most commonly affects the lungs, making pulmonary TB the classic and most frequent form. TB can also involve extrapulmonary sites such as the thyroid, pancreas, and myocardium, but these are rare.

High-yield Infectious Disease recall:
Pulmonary TB → most common manifestation of tuberculosis.
Extrapulmonary TB can involve lymph nodes, pleura, CNS, bones/joints, genitourinary tract, abdomen, and other organs.

Exam pearl:
TB can affect almost any organ, but the lung is the most common site.

Pathology 05.question: ৩৬) Cardiomyopathy occurs in which layer of heart?
Pathology 05.exp:
Cardiomyopathy is a disease of the heart muscle, i.e., the myocardium. It primarily affects the structure and function of cardiac muscle, leading to impaired contraction, relaxation, or both.

High-yield Cardiology recall:

  • Endocardium → inner lining of heart chambers

  • Myocardium → cardiac muscle; site of cardiomyopathy

  • Epicardium → outer layer of the heart wall

  • Pericardium → surrounding protective sac

Exam pearl:
“Cardio + myopathy = disease of cardiac muscle → myocardium.”

Pathology 05.question: ৩৭) Which one is tumor of heart?
Pathology 05.exp:
Cardiac myxoma is the most common primary benign tumor of the heart in adults. It most commonly arises in the left atrium, often from the interatrial septum near the fossa ovalis.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
Myxoma → most common primary cardiac tumor in adults → usually left atrium.

Exam pearl:
“Left atrial mass + classic primary cardiac tumor = Myxoma.”

Pathology 05.question: ৩৮) Which is a feature of primary tuberculosis?
Pathology 05.option2: both endogenous & exogenous source of infection
Pathology 05.exp:
Primary tuberculosis classically produces a subpleural parenchymal lesion (Ghon focus), usually in the lower part of the upper lobe or upper part of the lower lobe, with associated hilar lymph node involvement. Together, the primary pulmonary focus and involved regional lymph nodes form the Ghon complex.

High-yield Infectious Disease recall:

  • Primary TB → Ghon focus + hilar lymphadenopathy

  • Primary infection is more common in children and young individuals

  • It usually results from exogenous infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis

Exam pearl:
Primary TB → subpleural Ghon focus + hilar lymph nodes.

Pathology 05.question: ৩৯) Which virus is mostly responsible for congenital heart disease?
Pathology 05.exp:
Rubella virus is classically associated with congenital heart disease when maternal infection occurs during early pregnancy. Congenital rubella syndrome can cause patent ductus arteriosus (PDA), pulmonary artery stenosis, cataracts, and sensorineural deafness.

High-yield Pediatrics recall:
Congenital rubella syndrome → “PDA + cataract + deafness.”

Exam pearl:
Maternal rubella → congenital heart disease, classically PDA.

Pathology 05.question: ৪০) What type of necrosis is present in Ghon complex?
Pathology 05.exp:
The Ghon complex is a primary tuberculosis lesion consisting of a subpleural Ghon focus with regional hilar lymph node involvement. Tuberculous lesions characteristically show caseous necrosis, caused by a granulomatous immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

High-yield Pathology recall:
Tuberculosis → caseating granulomas → caseous necrosis.
A Ghon complex may heal by fibrosis and calcification, forming a Ranke complex.

Exam pearl:
“TB = caseous necrosis” → Ghon complex shows caseation.

Pathology 05.question: ৪১) Most of the tumors arising from lung are.....?
Pathology 05.exp:
Most primary malignant tumors arising in the lung are carcinomas, which originate from the epithelial lining of the respiratory tract. The major types include adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, small cell carcinoma, and large cell carcinoma.

High-yield Oncology recall:
Lung malignancies → predominantly epithelial carcinomas.
Among primary lung carcinomas, adenocarcinoma is currently the most common histologic type.

Exam pearl:
Most lung tumors = carcinomas, not sarcomas.

Pathology 05.question: ৪২) Which congenital heart disease is most common?
Pathology 05.exp:
Ventricular septal defect (VSD) is the most common congenital heart defect overall. It involves an abnormal opening in the interventricular septum, usually producing a left-to-right shunt.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
VSD → most common congenital heart defect.
A significant VSD can cause pulmonary overcirculation, left ventricular volume overload, and eventually pulmonary hypertension.

Exam pearl:
Most common congenital heart defect = VSD.

Pathology 05.question: ৪৩) What is the most common & important aetiological factor in development of lung cancer?
Pathology 05.exp:
Cigarette/tobacco smoking is the most important etiological factor for lung cancer. Tobacco smoke contains numerous carcinogens that cause repeated DNA damage and accumulation of genetic mutations in bronchial and pulmonary epithelial cells.

High-yield Oncology recall:
Smoking is strongly associated with:

  • Squamous cell carcinoma

  • Small cell carcinoma

  • Increased risk of other lung cancer subtypes

The risk increases with duration and intensity of smoking and decreases after cessation, although it does not immediately return to baseline.

Exam pearl:
Lung cancer + most important preventable cause → tobacco smoking.

Pathology 05.question: ৪৪) What is the most common mode of infection in lung abscess?
Pathology 05.exp:
Aspiration of infected oropharyngeal/gastric contents is the most common mechanism of lung abscess, especially in patients with impaired consciousness, poor swallowing or cough reflex, alcoholism, or anesthesia. Aspiration commonly affects dependent lung segments.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
Lung abscess → aspiration of infected material is the classic and most common mechanism.
Common organisms are often polymicrobial, including anaerobic oral flora.

Exam pearl:
Impaired consciousness + aspiration → lung abscess.

Pathology 05.question: ৪৫) Which lung tumor is more common in males?
Pathology 05.exp:
Historically, squamous cell carcinoma has been more common in males, largely because of its strong association with tobacco smoking. However, with changing smoking patterns, the sex difference has narrowed, and adenocarcinoma is now the most common lung cancer overall in both sexes.

High-yield Oncology recall:
Squamous cell carcinoma → strong smoking association → traditionally male predominance.
It often arises centrally near the major bronchi and may produce cavitation.

Exam pearl:
Traditional male-predominant lung carcinoma = squamous cell carcinoma.

Pathology 05.question: ৪৬) Which is an autoimmune disease?
Pathology 05.exp:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease in which the immune system attacks the synovial joints, causing persistent inflammation, pain, stiffness, and progressive joint destruction.

Osteoarthritis, osteomalacia, and osteoporosis are not primarily autoimmune diseases.

High-yield Rheumatology recall:
RA → autoimmune + inflammatory + systemic + chronic.

Exam pearl:
Autoimmune arthritis = Rheumatoid arthritis.

Pathology 05.question: ৪৭) Four features of TOF excludes.....?
Pathology 05.exp:
Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) has four classic features:

  1. Ventricular septal defect (VSD)

  2. Right ventricular outflow tract obstruction

  3. Overriding aorta

  4. Right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH)

Therefore, left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is not one of the four features.

High-yield Cardiology recall:
TOF = PROVe

  • Pulmonary/RV outflow obstruction

  • Right ventricular hypertrophy

  • Overriding aorta

  • VSD

Exam pearl:
TOF causes RVH, not LVH.

Pathology 05.question: ৪৮) Which is the most common fate of tuberculosis?
Pathology 05.exp:
The most common outcome of tuberculosis is healing, particularly when the host mounts an effective immune response. Tuberculous lesions may undergo fibrosis and calcification, producing a healed, inactive lesion.

In primary TB, a healed and calcified Ghon complex is termed a Ranke complex.

High-yield Infectious Disease recall:
TB → healing → fibrosis + calcification → inactive lesion.

Exam pearl:
Most TB lesions heal by fibrosis and calcification rather than progressive spread.

Pathology 05.question: ৪৯) Cough and sputum on most days for at least 3 months, in each of 2 consecutive years is called--?
Pathology 05.exp:
Chronic bronchitis is clinically defined as cough and sputum production on most days for at least 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years, after excluding other causes of chronic cough.

It is a common COPD phenotype, but COPD itself requires persistent airflow limitation on spirometry and is not defined solely by this symptom duration.

High-yield Respiratory recall:
3 months × 2 consecutive years = Chronic bronchitis.

Exam pearl:
“3 × 2 rule” → chronic bronchitis.

Pathology 05.question: ৫০) Consolidation occurs in which stage of pneumonia?
Pathology 05.exp:
In lobar pneumonia, the red hepatization stage is characterized by consolidation of the affected lung. The alveoli become filled with red blood cells, neutrophils, and fibrin, making the lung firm and liver-like.

The classical stages are:

  1. Congestion

  2. Red hepatization → consolidation

  3. Gray hepatization

  4. Resolution

High-yield Pathology recall:
Red hepatization → alveolar consolidation → RBCs + neutrophils + fibrin.

Exam pearl:
“Red hepatization = consolidated, liver-like lung.”
